title: ALMA image of the protoplanetary disc around HL Tauri
caption: The protoplanetary disc around HL Tauri, imaged by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
celestial: HL Tauri · constellation Taurus · about 450 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #54 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This is the disc of material surrounding the young star HL Tauri, seen by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in what ESO describes as the sharpest image the observatory had ever taken. Dark patches lie within the disc, and ALMA revealed substructures there that had never been seen before.

A protoplanetary disc is the flattened ring of gas and dust around a newborn star, the raw material from which planets are thought to form. The detail here is sharper than the Hubble Space Telescope routinely achieves in visible light, and that sharpness is what lets such fine structure show up.

Most intriguing of all, the observations may show where planets are taking shape, since the dark patches could mark the positions of planets in the process of forming. ALMA works at millimeter wavelengths, picking up a faint glow from the disc that visible-light telescopes cannot see.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (0.03 x 0.03 arcminutes) and distance (450 light years), the frame spans roughly 0 × 0 light-years. Its light set out about 450 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: ALMA observed this disc in millimeter-wavelength light, at 1.28 mm. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Millimeter-wavelength light is invisible to the eye, so this picture is a rendering of that signal rather than a view anyone could see through an eyepiece.

explore: HL Tauri lies about 450 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Taurus. ALMA is an array of many antennas that work together as a single telescope, and this view was made at a wavelength of 1.28 millimeters.
alt: The disc around the young star HL Tauri, with dark patches within it.
